text:
Marathon Petroleum stock bounced 4.6% today after falling hard over the prior week, driven by easing geopolitical tension. News that U.S. Secretary of State Rubio saw "little hope" of a diplomatic breakthrough with Iran may sound negative, but it signals the market is pricing in a lower risk of imminent oil supply disruptions from Middle East conflict—a concern that had weighed heavily on the stock during last week's sharper decline. Oil prices remain elevated (U.S. crude at $99.64/barrel), but the removal of shock-disruption fear helped refiners like Marathon recover some ground.

The broader context is that refiners live on the spread between crude costs and fuel prices; they profit when they can buy oil and sell gasoline and diesel for a wider margin. Last week's steep drop reflected fears of supply shock and uncertainty, but today's bounce suggests those extreme-case worries have eased slightly, at least for now. Refineries are still running near full capacity (94.5%), so there's room for the business to keep running profitably if crude-to-fuel spreads hold steady.
